summary: 18 criteria pass; R1, R11, R16, R17 and R22 fail because protected operations can continue using cached workspace configuration after delivery policy or repository scope changes during execution.

criteria.title: Planning and milestone authority
criteria.explanation: Planning approvals, validation and milestone predicates are implemented. However, the merge boundary can admit stale repository policy after the workspace configuration changes during hosted-check waiting; F1 prevents the required rejection of all invalid passage.
evidence: plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/current/actions.js:83 — post-wait checks retain the original core context

criteria.title: Model-led execution
criteria.explanation: Readiness records intent without launching evaluation. Explicit execution requests select gates without a scheduling DAG, retain genuine consumed-evidence requirements, and impose no remediation-round limit.

criteria.title: Canonical layouts
criteria.explanation: The resolver and local object store support repository-local and shared-parent records without requiring evidence commits. Fixtures cover untracked records, tracked/ignored parent records and local integration/finalization.

criteria.title: Exact source and requirements
criteria.explanation: Candidates retain exact requirement bytes, approval references and independently captured base/head/target source. Feature scope requires the configured original base and complete rubric; admission validates retained bytes and live source.

criteria.title: Containment and isolation
criteria.explanation: Canonical reads reject traversal, unsafe ancestors, symlinks and replacement. Reviewer exports contain selected retained source, requirements and explicit evidence, filter reserved history, and use fresh read-only evaluator requests with network-deny policy.

criteria.title: Publication and retention
criteria.explanation: Exclusive publication rejects conflicting bytes; mirrored journals and outcome markers support repeat/crash reconciliation. Missing or corrupt evidence blocks qualification, and retention preserves failures without claiming backup or introducing automatic pruning.

criteria.title: Local finalization
criteria.explanation: Packet inventories derive from recorded, qualified references and local closure validation. Application cleanliness, pinned source and PR synchronization checks remain separate; executable/configuration files cannot hide behind evidence-directory names.

criteria.title: Independent grouped verdicts
criteria.explanation: Grouped code/spec execution validates each verdict separately and rejects missing verdicts or unqualified contexts. The embedded actual evaluator receipt was independently checked with the pinned public validator and its output digest matched.
evidence: Read-only public validation returned PASS for context 01a16cc8-7243-7180-91b2-9329b2bccd42 and output digest sha256:ebc8c5acd8501e78729ba56caf46e4378e3a76b5666fb0f2dc81c2bf812c41dd

criteria.title: Complete obligation inventory
criteria.explanation: The C1 obligations remain explicit, including separate Judge, code/spec, reconciliation, explanation, packet and completion obligations. Runner PASS requires successful receipts for every declared check; optional Whiteboard retains its policy.
evidence: .gatereeve-agent-evidence/patches/feature.json — inspected removal of the previous obligation model

criteria.title: Equivalent-input reuse
criteria.explanation: Content applicability excludes incidental commit identity while retaining relevant source, scope and requirement content. Reuse returns original result references and execution provenance, with fixtures checking unchanged-tree and bookkeeping changes.

criteria.title: Relevant change and uncertainty
criteria.explanation: Source, requirement, environment, dependency and consumed-proof mutations have substantial checks. Workspace repository configuration is nevertheless compared against cached objects, so a relevant on-disk policy/scope change can remain equivalent during an ongoing operation.
evidence: cli/test/current-core.test.js:2395 — configuration test changes the in-memory context

criteria.title: Targeted delta coverage
criteria.explanation: Delta execution requires recorded qualifying prior proof, compatible requirements/scope, all changed paths and explicit interaction coverage. Base-only and target-only changes enter the delta, and original provenance remains retained.

criteria.title: Bounded history and dispositions
criteria.explanation: Packets distinguish claims, reviewer reports, coverage limits and unavailable history. Open/claimed findings require supported dispositions; changed closures require an independent relevance assessment, while unaffected closures can be carried together.

criteria.title: New discovery and blocking criteria
criteria.explanation: Reviewer instructions expressly permit new supported defects and new instances of resolved classes. Blocking findings require an approved criterion or gate rule and an in-scope source path; unrelated findings do not automatically supersede applicable proof.

criteria.title: One scoped human decision
criteria.explanation: Observed instructions retain quote/context and available provenance. Combined waiver/amendment continuations use durable pending records and repeat-safe operations, retain old/new commitments, and do not require another approval for identical retries.

criteria.title: Honest exceptions and integration
criteria.explanation: Original outcomes, exceptions and observed integration remain distinct, and waivers do not imply merge authority. However, F1 allows previously authorized actions to execute after repository policy/scope drift that should invalidate their applicability.

criteria.title: Enforcement coverage
criteria.explanation: Hook coverage is honestly labeled and direct merge commands route to the protected adapter. The adapter's post-wait checks do not reload workspace configuration, leaving the reachable invalid-action path in F1.

criteria.title: Coherent consumers and low ceremony
criteria.explanation: CLI, native adapter and Desktop consume the current core view. Ordering controls and manual PASS transport are removed; operations generate routine records. The bound Verification reports current consumer/build smoke, supported by the inspected runtime image.

criteria.title: Direct cutover
criteria.explanation: Current entrypoints use one protocol; retired orchestration files and Desktop scheduler interfaces are removed. Unsupported operations/receipts are rejected with current-entry guidance. Remaining historical release readers do not provide an old feature-workflow interpreter.
evidence: cli/test/local-agent-adapters.test.js — old receipt requests are rejected

criteria.title: Resume without false history
criteria.explanation: Resume establishes durable current runs and explicit observed approvals without replaying old journals. Unsupported activation records remain retained provenance; interrupted activation and outcomes reconcile without inheriting historical PASS or overwriting old files.

criteria.title: Practical observations
criteria.explanation: Retained receipts expose execution timestamps, outcomes and available usage/cost data through result reads. Missing metric contributions remain null, known zero remains zero, and workflow guidance calls for real-project observation without a benchmark gate.
evidence: cli/test/local-agent-adapters.test.js — incomplete usage contributions remain unknown

criteria.title: Scoped standing acceptance and merge
criteria.explanation: Standing grants enforce explicit scope, actual gate PASS, exact merge actions, expiry and revocation. But their repository-configuration binding is recomputed from cached context rather than the current configuration file, so configuration drift during execution does not reliably invalidate derived authority.

criteria.title: Standing authority surfaces and PR default
criteria.explanation: Current views expose grant scope, applications and inactive reasons. CLI and Desktop render these records, open drafts remain the default, and explicitly configured closed PRs retain their protected merge-window behavior.

markdown:
**FAIL — 18 criteria pass and 5 fail.** One supported defect affects R1, R11, R16, R17 and R22: protected operations retain stale workspace configuration during execution.

The assessment covers the complete FEATURE_FINAL source from `643e3ea2b03f19b66595219c4f8df934596aa436` to `6d36117b1ad007141647b2739b4b6a1af9f45269`, all 23 approved rubric rows, the specification/design including D11, and the full bound Verification report.

Evidence integrity checks passed: the inventory contains 327 changes (105 modified, 157 deleted, 65 added), no binary entries, and all present changed files match their declared Git blob identities. All 53 patch chunks and their assembled digest matched. Desktop's 24 protocol files and canonical non-test Python helpers match their staged copies. `runtime.png` was verified and inspected. The embedded actual evaluator receipt passed the pinned public validator, including its output digest. The broader implementation suites were assessed through supplied Verification evidence, not rerun.

For the references below, `P/` means `plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/current/`, and `T` means `cli/test/current-core.test.js`.

**F1 — Cached workspace configuration permits stale-policy merge execution.**

The native adapter resolves `.agentic-workflow.json` once when a request starts (`P/adapter.js:92`). `CurrentCore` stores that result and later returns copies of the same repository configuration (`P/core.js:70`). Candidate checks compare against this cached configuration (`P/evidence.js:203`), as do standing-grant bindings (`P/authorization.js:47`).

A reachable case is a valid protected merge waiting in `gh pr checks --watch`. During that wait, change the selected repository's integration/release branch or `keepPullRequestsClosed` policy in `.agentic-workflow.json`. The subsequent checks at `P/actions.js:83` still use the old configuration and can reach `gh pr merge` at line 104. Removing the repository or reassigning its configured path is similarly invisible to the in-flight core. A shared-parent configuration need not belong to Git; a repository-root configuration is explicitly excluded from source checks (`P/evidence.js:26`).

This is an omitted live-input check throughout the operation, rather than merely the unavoidable interval after a final filesystem observation. D11 explicitly requires repository configuration drift to invalidate further use, including already derived but unexecuted merges (`design.md:344`; `spec.md:299`). The existing configuration test changes `f.context.repositories` directly (`T:2395`), so it does not establish detection of the actual file-change scenario. This finding follows the pinned source path; no hosted or destructive reproduction was performed.

| R22 | FAIL | Explicit scope, actual PASS, expiry/revocation and exact actions are checked, but on-disk repository-configuration drift is not requalified during execution. `P/authorization.js:43`, `P/authorization.js:73`, `P/actions.js:83`; D11. |

**Scope check: PASS.** Changed work remains within the approved core, helpers, schemas, consumers, tests, documentation and generated projections. Whole-feature scope was retained.

**Gap check: FAIL.** Protected operations lack live workspace-configuration revalidation. The configuration test mutates an in-memory object, and the formal final mutation matrix does not cover the configuration-file change during hosted waiting.

**Contradiction check: FAIL.** Cached configuration after hosted waiting contradicts approved D11's required invalidation on repository configuration drift.

The Verification report is explicitly composite. Its actual ARM64 application smoke and retained evaluator execution are useful evidence; its fixture transports and historical checks do not establish a real hosted merge, installed-host interception, native Intel execution or publication. Those disclosed limits are not additional pre-merge failures.
